text:
ashley: Heads-up — after the kernel selector change rolled yesterday we're seeing steady memory growth on Qwen-Long runs (rope scaling > 1.5). Repro on dedicated2. Dedicated load: longprefix + multi-turn chat. Symptoms: pages get pinned and evictions aren't freeing the expected slabs. Not a full OOM yet but sustained growth over 30m.

matt: Can you paste the smallest repro + perf snippet? I can run on my rig.

ashley: repro command below, very small:
```bash
# hit the longprefix path (~50k tokens across loops)
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN" \\  -d '{"model":"qwen-long-1.1","input":"<long prompt>" ,"max_tokens":2048,"prefill_mode":"longprefix"}'
```

ashley: core telemetry extract (abridged):
```
kv_cache.total_pages: 12432
kv_cache.pinned_pages: 312
kv_cache.evict_attempts: 24123
kv_cache.evicted_pages: 312
kv_cache.fragmentation_pct: 18.7
kernel_selector: gqa_mqa_opt_v2
queued_batch_window_ms: 4
```

zhen: I grabbed a flamegraph from yesterday's canary  — hot path is split between `kv_reconcile` and `gqa_postprocess`. There's a surprising number of tiny allocations inside `kv_reconcile` that correlate with page pin increments. Looks like the kernel switch changed the update ordering so some pages are re-pinned during postprocess instead of after eviction.

zhen: flamegraph summary: `kv_reconcile` (32%) -> `gqa_postprocess` (21%) -> `memcpy` (9%) -> `rope_rescale` (6%). 

ashley: also note behavior differs between MQA and GQA variants: with MQA we saw more contiguous reuse (lower fragmentation) but GQA path does the per-block remap that leaves lots of small free slots. Combined with our slab layout it prevents coalescing, so eviction only frees tiny fragments that aren't useful for longprefix allocations.

sara: quick mitigation: revert to old kernel_selector for requests that set `prefill_mode: longprefix` and bump `queued_batch_window_ms` to 8ms for the canary. That should reduce re-pin races and give the eviction background worker more time to coalesce. Canary today? :eyes:

matt: I'll run the repro locally with the old selector and the bump. If we see stable memory it's a strong signal kernel ordering is the root.

ashley: attaching a small trace snippet (simplified):
```
[request start]
  -> allocate prefills
  -> kernel gqa_mqa_opt_v2: write kv pages (set pin++ per slot)
  -> postprocess: readback touches same slots -> pin++ again (bug: no decrement after prefetch fail)
  -> eviction worker: sees fragments but can't coalesce due to interleaved pins
[request end]
```

zhen: There's a subtle interaction with rope scaling: when rope>1 the effective key offset moves slots across slab boundaries, increasing fragmentation since remap maps to different slab indices. Our slab allocator assumes locality, so rope remap skews that. I can reproduce a worst-case by toggling rope_scale=1.7 in the perf harness.

matt: repro note: when I toggled rope_scale locally and used Qwen-Long MQA vs GQA, only GQA showed the persistent growth. MQA still reuses. So it's not purely slab allocator, it's kernel's remap policy + ordering.

perf-bot: Canary deployment started for canary/dedicated2 with kernel_selector=fallback_v1 and queued_batch_window_ms=8 at 1717866900.

devops-bot: Dedicated instance dedicated2-03 hit an OOM at 1717867001, container restarted. Crash log: `OOM killer: kv_cache exceeded budget -> killed process`. Rolling logs attached in the ops ticket.

sara: Ugh. That OOM came during a burst before the canary global split was fully propagated. Can we isolate the dedicated host and re-run with strict rate limit on that host?

ashley: yes we throttled traffic to dedicated2-03 and started a reduced-rate run. Early numbers look better: pinned_pages dropped from ~312 -> ~40 over 12m on the fallback kernel.

zhen: I also ran a microbenchmark patch that moves the decrement of prefetch pins into a safer post-io path and adds a small batching window for pin updates. Results: fragmentation pct drops by ~6-8% and steady-state pinned_pages down ~60%. I'll open a PR with the change and perf numbers.

matt: please include a test that toggles rope_scale across 1.0/1.5/1.8 and asserts no growth beyond threshold after 20m. That will catch regressions.

ashley: agree — also add an eviction coalescing metric to telemetry so we can watch in prod (coalesce_attempts, coalesce_success). Right now we only have evict_attempts/evicted_pages which don't highlight failed coalesce attempts.

sara: Next steps summary:
- revert kernel_selector for longprefix path (done canary)
- add coalesce telemetry (sara -> infra)
- land zhen's pin-decrement patch behind flag + perf tests (zhen)
- add rope_scale soak tests in perf harness + CI (matt)

ashley: thanks everyone. If the canary stays stable I'll schedule the kernel selector rollback to stable tomorrow morning. I'll follow up in ops ticket with final numbers. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Canary run complete: memory growth stopped for 90% of runs, 10% noisy outliers flagged for postmortem. (ticket #OPS-4321)

devops-bot: cleaned and restarted dedicated2-03 at 1717867540. Host back online.
